name: Stone World
tagline: Push the rune stones home. No timers, no lives.
description: A push box puzzle in pixel art: push rune stones onto an ancient altar, take keys from chests and open gates across 20 hand-made chambers.
storeDescription: Stone World is a Sokoban-style puzzle game in pixel art. In each chamber you push rune stones onto an ancient altar, take keys from chests and open the gates in the way, and when every rune is lit the portal to the next chamber opens. A stone only moves when you push it, so a stone pushed into a corner stays there, and restarting is always one tap away. There are 20 hand-made chambers, no timers and no lives, and everything works offline. The game is free, with a full-screen ad after every fifth chamber and one optional purchase that opens every chamber and removes the ads.

features.title: 20 hand-made chambers
features.description: From a first lesson to a finale with four keys and four gates. Each chamber adds one idea to the one before it and opens once you solve it.

features.title: Runes, keys and gates
features.description: Light the altar one rune stone at a time, take keys from chests and spend each one on a gate. A key used on the wrong gate is gone.

features.title: Courtyards and terraces
features.description: Later chambers join courtyards and terraces with stairs, where a stone can only go where you can follow it.

features.title: Controls made for exact moves
features.description: Tap an arrow to move exactly one cell, hold it to keep walking, or touch anywhere on the screen to bring the joystick under your thumb.

features.title: Calm and offline
features.description: No timers, no lives and no connection needed. Agate, a stone guide, gives a short hint as you enter, and the first chambers show the way with blue motes.

buildStory.problem: I started Stone World in Unity in 2021: a main menu, a rune counter and stones that were plain physics bodies you could shove around freely. Then it sat untouched for years. In 2026 I wanted to finish it instead of starting something new.
buildStory.solution: I moved it to Unity 6 with URP 2D and changed the stones so a push moves them exactly one cell on a grid, which made the puzzles possible to design at all. Each chamber is built by an editor script, and a breadth-first solver over pushes proves it solvable before it ships, then a Play Mode walkthrough replays that solution in the real scene. The art comes from licensed pixel art packs.
buildStory.learned: I tried generating chambers from seeds and scoring them, and deleted all ten: they were solvable but did not follow on from one another. The ones that shipped are placed by hand and checked by the solver, and proving the last chamber took 13 minutes and 1.7 million states. The first release was also a 45 MB download, and stripping unused code, turning off the splash and removing a post-processing stack the game no longer used brought it to 35.6 MB.

name: Love Wrapped
tagline: Your chat, told back as a love story.
description: Turns a WhatsApp chat between two people into a Wrapped of the relationship, one scene per screen, and a vertical video, all on the phone.
storeDescription: Love Wrapped reads a WhatsApp chat export between two people and tells the story back as a Wrapped: the first messages, the first "I love you", the longest run of days in a row, the hours and words that are yours. The chat is read on the phone and never uploaded, only the numbers of the story are kept, and there is no account to create. The story can be renamed and reordered, then turned into a 9:16 video with an original soundtrack. No ads, and one optional lifetime Premium through Google Play unlocks every scene and the full 1080p video without the watermark.

features.title: Read on the phone
features.description: The chat is parsed on the device and the app deletes its copy when the reading ends. Only the story's numbers are saved, never the messages.

features.title: One discovery per screen
features.description: Scenes are picked from what the chat really holds, from the first messages shown as lock screen notifications to milestones, laughs and emoji.

features.title: About the couple
features.description: It never ranks who texts more, who replies faster or who says sorry, and it never brings back a bad moment.

features.title: Make it yours
features.description: Change the names, reorder or hide scenes. Premium adds a color per scene and a photo of the two of you behind the first messages.

features.title: A video to share
features.description: A 9:16 MP4 with an original soundtrack, rendered on the phone, or a single scene as an image. The free video is 720p with a watermark.

buildStory.problem: A recap of a relationship needs the whole WhatsApp conversation, which is about the most private file on a phone. The reading had to happen on the device, and the export looks different on Android and iPhone and in each language.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app with a hand-written, pure-Dart parser that streams the export in an isolate and lets only aggregates out; a 200,000-message chat read in about five seconds in my tests. A scene engine scores each possible scene against those numbers, and one CustomPainter draws the viewer and every video frame, which a Kotlin MediaCodec encoder turns into H.264 with an AAC soundtrack.
buildStory.learned: The rule that shaped the engine is to never invent data: a scene that cannot back its sentence with the chat's numbers is dropped. Drawing the preview and the video with the same painter also means the story you watch is the video you share.

name: Poker Trainer
tagline: Texas Hold'em, one short lesson at a time.
description: No Limit Hold'em lessons for beginners: 58 lessons in 13 phases, over 400 exercises and an explanation after every answer. No real money.
storeDescription: Poker Trainer teaches No Limit Texas Hold'em in lessons of three to five minutes, from hand rankings to push or fold in tournaments. Each exercise is one decision, followed by a short explanation with the cards that matter lit up. The 58 lessons in 13 phases are bundled in the app, work offline and come in English and Portuguese. There is no real money and chips are never sold. Every lesson is free, there are no ads, and one optional purchase removes the wait for lives.

features.title: 13 phases
features.description: 58 lessons from the Kitchen Table to the Final Table. Each phase ends with a challenge that mixes everything it taught.

features.title: Real decisions
features.description: Act at the table, name the hand, pick the winner at showdown, complete a hand, count outs, or answer a quick question.

features.title: Why, after every answer
features.description: A short explanation with the cards that decide it lit up. A wrong answer comes back at the end of the lesson, and the summary points out the mistakes you repeat.

features.title: Streak, XP, lives and chips
features.description: A daily habit, like a language app. Lives refill over time or with chips earned in lessons. Chips are never sold and there is no real money.

features.title: Practice and hand rankings
features.description: Free practice on any lesson already unlocked, without spending lives, and a hand rankings sheet with how often each hand comes up in seven cards.

buildStory.problem: Poker study material is long, dense and far from the table. A beginner who knows some rules and plays by feel tends to give up before the concepts stick.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app shaped like a language app: short lessons, one decision per exercise, a path of phases that unlock in order. The content is bundled JSON in English and Portuguese, progress stays on the phone, and the only network use is Firebase Analytics, a Google Play Games leaderboard and the purchase, none of which blocks the app.
buildStory.learned: Authored answers cannot be trusted. A Node validator with its own hand evaluator scores every hand-based answer and checks that both languages match exercise by exercise, and a Dart port of it decides which cards light up after an answer. Keeping chips off sale was deliberate: chips sold for money in a poker app read as simulated gambling.

name: Scoreboard
tagline: The score, readable from across the court.
description: Scoreboard for two teams, Blue and Red, with +1, +5 or tennis scoring, sets or a timed clock, exact undo and the score on your watch.
storeDescription: Scoreboard keeps the score of a match between two teams, Blue and Red. Instead of a list of sports, the first launch asks how you play: +1, +5 or tennis scoring, sets or a timed match with a clock, a deciding set, a golden point and team rotation. Tap a side to score, undo the exact last change, swap sides, hear the score out loud and add points from a watch or the lock screen. It works offline, with no account, no ads and nothing to buy.

features.title: Rules, not sports
features.description: No list of sports to pick from. Answer once how you play: points per set, best of how many, deciding set, two-point lead, tennis games and tiebreaks, or periods on a clock.

features.title: Exact undo
features.description: Undo reverses the last change exactly, not just the number. Hold a team's score to set it on a wheel, or hold undo to start over.

features.title: Score from your watch
features.description: On Android the score shows up as a playing track on a watch or the lock screen. Previous and next add a point to each side, and the middle button undoes.

features.title: Team rotation
features.description: Winner stays and loser leaves, and after 2, 3 or 4 wins in a row the winner leaves too. A draw sends both teams off.

features.title: Made for the court
features.description: Score read out loud, sound and vibration on each point, the screen kept awake, a landscape lock, and the match saved on every change.

buildStory.problem: Our pickup volleyball has its own rules, like a deciding set to 15 and a winner who leaves after a few wins in a row. A scoreboard built around a list of sports cannot describe a game like that.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app for Android and iOS where a match is described by the answers to a short onboarding instead of a sport. The score is never stored: a match is its rules plus a list of events, and a pure engine replays them into the current score. No backend, no login, only Firebase Analytics.
buildStory.learned: Storing events instead of the score made undo exact, since it only drops the last event, and it lets a match survive the app being killed. The fiddly part was the watch: Android drops bursts of notification updates, so the silent media session that reaches Wear OS coalesces them every 250 ms.

name: Tomely
description: Medication reminder that rings on time, even offline, keeps a dose history and warns you before a medication runs out.
storeDescription: Add a medication once and Tomely rings at every dose. Confirm or postpone straight from the notification, follow your day split into morning, afternoon and evening, and see a history of everything you took. It counts your pills and warns you before they run out. No ads, no subscription.

features.title: Reminders on time
features.description: An alarm at every dose, with sound and vibration. If you do not confirm, it reminds you again, and it keeps working without internet.

features.title: Any schedule
features.description: Every day, some weekdays, every X days or every X hours, several doses a day, each with its own amount and instructions.

features.title: History and streaks
features.description: Every dose logged with the time you took it, a 7-day adherence chart and a streak of days without a missed dose.

features.title: Stock alerts
features.description: Tomely counts what is left and warns you before a medication runs out, so the refill is not a surprise.

buildStory.problem: Medication reminders are most useful to people who struggle with small text and busy screens, and most apps in the Brazilian market are built for people who already live on their phones.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app designed for adults from 25 to 60+, with large touch targets and text, reminders scheduled on the device with exact alarms, and data synced to a Firebase account so it survives a new phone.
buildStory.learned: Health data changes every decision. The account ID never reaches Analytics or Crashlytics, logs are scrubbed before they leave the phone, and deleting the account erases everything from inside the app.

name: FlyControl
tagline: Your Fly.io apps, in your pocket.
description: Unofficial Fly.io client to check apps and machines, read live logs, follow CPU and memory, and restart a machine from your phone.
storeDescription: FlyControl is an unofficial Fly.io client for Android. It shows whether your apps and machines are running and lets you act on them from your phone: start, stop or restart a machine, follow its logs and read its CPU, memory, network and disk charts. It signs in with a Fly.io organization token that stays in encrypted storage on the device and is sent only to the Fly.io API. Not affiliated with Fly.io.

features.title: Apps and machines
features.description: Every app in your organization with its status, machine count and regions. Filter machines by state and search by ID, app or region.

features.title: Act from your phone
features.description: Start, stop or restart a machine. Destroying one asks for confirmation first.

features.title: Live logs
features.description: Follow the log stream of an app or a single machine, filter by level and copy any line.

features.title: Metrics
features.description: CPU, memory, network and disk charts from the last hour to the last 30 days, plus recent deployments.

features.title: Token stays on the phone
features.description: Several accounts and organizations, stored in encrypted storage and sent to the Fly.io API and nowhere else.

buildStory.problem: Checking whether a Fly.io machine was up, or reading its logs, meant opening a laptop. The web dashboard is not made for a phone.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter client for Android and iOS that talks directly to the Machines API, the GraphQL API and the Prometheus metrics endpoint, with no server and no account of its own.
buildStory.learned: Most of the work was in the API, not the UI: undocumented endpoints, rate limits and refresh intervals chosen so the app stays fresh without hammering Fly.io.

name: CAM Covers
tagline: Make your photos look like real music album covers.
description: Turns a photo into a music player screen with your own song title and artist, ready to share.
storeDescription: CAM Covers turns your photos into music album covers inspired by real music players, from a grunge rock album to a dreamy lo-fi single. Pick a player style, drop in a photo, type the song title and artist, and share the result on Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook or TikTok. Everything is rendered on your phone, with no account.

features.title: Six player styles
features.description: Green, Red, Minimalist, Blur, Anime and Metal, each inspired by a real music player.

features.title: Your text, your colours
features.description: Edit the song title, the artist and the extra line, and change the player colour.

features.title: Gallery or camera
features.description: Pick a photo or take one, then crop it to fit the cover.

features.title: Save and share
features.description: Save to the gallery or send it through the share sheet to Instagram Stories, TikTok or WhatsApp.

buildStory.problem: I tried to create an album cover montage manually on Instagram and it took forever: stickers, manual cropping, several apps. There had to be a faster way.
buildStory.solution: An app that uses Flutter's own rendering system as the editing canvas. RenderRepaintBoundary captures the live UI as a high-resolution image, so no image manipulation library was needed. Flutter itself became the editor.
buildStory.learned: AI-assisted template creation cut 8 hours of design work to under 1 hour. I used Claude 3.5 via Cursor to generate 4 templates from 2 existing ones. The lesson: think about what parts of your product can be accelerated with AI before writing them from scratch.

name: Direção Fácil
tagline: Pass your CNH exam. 5 minutes a day.
description: Gamified app to help Brazilians pass the CNH theory exam with short lessons and DETRAN-style quizzes.
storeDescription: Direção Fácil is the complete app for passing the theory test of the Brazilian driver's license (CNH) and actually learning traffic law. Study by topic in learning trails, practise with DETRAN-style questions based on the traffic code, and see which topics still cost you points. The real test has 30 multiple-choice questions and you pass with 21. Not affiliated with DETRAN, SENATRAN or any government agency.

features.title: DETRAN-style practice
features.description: Questions based on the Brazilian Traffic Code (CTB), in the format of the official test. Take as many as you want.

features.title: Themed trails
features.description: Legislation, road signs, defensive driving, first aid, basic mechanics, and infractions and penalties, in an order that builds on itself.

features.title: Performance tracking
features.description: Your progress in each topic, so you know where to focus before a weak area costs you points on the test.

features.title: Gamified progress
features.description: XP, levels, streaks, daily quests and achievements, plus a weekly heat map of your study days.

features.title: Lives
features.description: Up to five lives that refill over time. Watch an ad for one more, or go Premium for unlimited lives.

buildStory.problem: Studying for the CNH theoretical exam in Brazil is boring, dense, and most people fail on the first try because the study materials are awful.
buildStory.solution: A gamified study app modeled after Duolingo: short lessons, quizzes and trails covering the topics of the official exam.
buildStory.learned: Gamification only works when the core learning loop is solid. Points and levels are motivators, not substitutes for well-structured content.

name: Idle Elevator
tagline: How high can your elevator go?
description: Idle clicker game where you manage an elevator that never stops climbing. Upgrade attributes, collect coins, and unlock prestige bonuses.
storeDescription: Idle Elevator is an idle clicker game where you manage an elevator that climbs endlessly. Tap to earn extra coins while the elevator rises automatically, pick up passengers for a 3x income bonus, chain combos to multiply earnings, and hit BOOST to accelerate the elevator by 5x. Invest in Speed, Capacity and Profit upgrades, buying in bulk with 10x, 100x or MAX. Reach enough floors to unlock prestige and restart with permanent income bonuses. Your elevator keeps earning offline for up to 4 hours.

features.title: Endless Climb
features.description: The elevator rises automatically. Tap the building for extra coins and pick up passengers for a 3x income bonus.

features.title: Combos & Boost
features.description: Chain combos to multiply your earnings and activate BOOST to accelerate the elevator by 5x.

features.title: Three Upgrade Paths
features.description: Invest in Speed, Capacity and Profit. Buy upgrades individually or in bulk with 10x, 100x or MAX.

features.title: Prestige System
features.description: Reach enough floors to unlock prestige and restart with permanent income bonuses that compound run after run.

features.title: Offline Earnings
features.description: Your elevator keeps working for up to 4 hours while the app is closed. Collect the coins when you return, and double them.

buildStory.problem: I wanted to explore the idle/incremental genre, games where progression keeps happening even when the player isn't actively playing, and ship a polished version of one.
buildStory.solution: An elevator-themed idle clicker with three upgrade trees, a prestige loop, and offline earnings. The elevator metaphor maps naturally to vertical progression, which makes the core loop intuitive on first open.
buildStory.learned: Idle games live or die by their numbers. Tuning the cost curves and prestige multipliers took longer than building the entire UI: the game has to feel rewarding at minute 1 and still be motivating at hour 10.

name: The Slime Dungeon
tagline: Surrounded by adorable danger. How long can you last?
description: Survive in a dungeon full of slimes! You are stuck with adorable creatures. How long can you survive?
storeDescription: You wake up trapped in a dungeon filled with slimes: cute, relentless and closing in. Move with the joystick, aim your fireballs and keep an eye on your stamina. Open chests for potions, survive the growing waves and put your score on the Google Play Games leaderboard. Built with Flutter and the Bonfire game engine.

features.title: Survival Gameplay
features.description: Waves of slimes that keep growing. Big slimes are worth 5 points, small ones 3. Stay alive as long as you can.

features.title: Fireballs and stamina
features.description: Aim with the joystick and fire, but every shot costs stamina.

features.title: Chests and potions
features.description: Red restores life, blue gives a temporary shield, green is poison.

features.title: Leaderboard
features.description: Sign in with Google Play Games, if you want, to compare your best run with other players.

buildStory.problem: I wanted to build a mobile game that was genuinely fun to play, not just a tutorial project I'd never open again.
buildStory.solution: A survival dungeon game with a single twist: the enemies are cute slimes. Used Flutter with the Bonfire engine, which gave me RPG-style game mechanics without writing a full engine from scratch.
buildStory.learned: Game feel matters more than graphics. Getting the movement and hit detection right took longer than building the entire visual layer. Bonfire made the RPG primitives easy; the hard part was tuning the difficulty curve.

name: Virtual Pocket Air Conditioning
tagline: An air conditioner hum, in your pocket.
description: A virtual air conditioner in your pocket: one button, a wind animation and the continuous hum of an AC unit.
storeDescription: Virtual Pocket Air Conditioning turns your phone into a pretend air conditioner. Press the power button and the hum of an AC unit fades in, with cool air waves on screen. It does not cool anything, but plenty of people sleep better with that sound in the background. Built as a fun project to study animations in Flutter.

features.title: AC sound
features.description: A looped air conditioner hum that fades in when you turn it on and fades out when you turn it off.

features.title: Wind animation
features.description: The AC pulses and cool air waves drift across the screen while it runs.

features.title: One button
features.description: Power on, power off. Nothing else to configure.

features.title: Nothing collected
features.description: No ads, no account, no internet access. The only permission keeps the sound playing.

buildStory.problem: I couldn't sleep without background noise. Air conditioning units are expensive and not always available, so I built a virtual one.
buildStory.solution: A small Flutter app that plays a looped AC ambient sound. The project also served as a sandbox for experimenting with animations in Flutter.
buildStory.learned: The apps users keep are the ones that do one thing extremely well. No feature creep needed.

name: Ciclogravura
tagline: Sand art inside a glass bottle.
description: A game based on the Brazilian sand bottle craft: pour colored sand, tilt the phone and shape landscapes against the glass, grain by grain.
storeDescription: Ciclogravura is a portrait game based on a craft from the Brazilian Northeast: drawing landscapes inside a glass bottle with colored sand. Pour sand through a straw, tilt the phone to make the layers slide, push them with a skewer, take some out with a spoon and set small items inside. Free mode has no goal and no score, and the campaign asks you to recreate a reference landscape and grades your bottle in stars. Some bottles and items open after a rewarded video you choose to watch, and one optional lifetime Premium through Google Play opens all of them, skips the videos and removes the watermark from shared pictures.

features.title: Straw, skewer and spoon
features.description: Pour with the straw, shape with the skewer and remove with the spoon, in 14 sand colors, with undo at any time.

features.title: Real tilt
features.description: The sand runs as you turn the phone, read from the accelerometer, or with the tilt buttons on screen.

features.title: Free mode and collection
features.description: No goal and no rush. Finished bottles go into a collection, each with the weight of sand it took, and can be shared as a picture.

features.title: Campaign
features.description: Two worlds and 9 levels, such as the backlands, a raft and the Lençóis dunes. Each bottle is compared with the reference and earns one to five stars.

features.title: Bottles and items
features.description: 9 bottle shapes and 9 items, like a shell, a palm tree and a cactus, set inside with tweezers and held in place by the sand around them.

buildStory.problem: Falling-sand toys usually treat sand like a liquid: it levels out and any shape you carve collapses. In the real craft the artisan carves hills and skies against the glass with a thin rod, so the game had to let that work stay in place.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app with a Flame loop over a pure-Dart grid of 160 by 260 cells, one grain per cell, stepped a fixed 100 times a second. Grains speed up as they fall, hold on 20% of the time so slopes collapse in small avalanches and rest near 32 degrees, and grains pressed by the skewer only fall straight down, which is what keeps a carved shape. The skewer follows the palheta used in Majorlândia: it sinks the upper color into the layer below and never swaps cells.
buildStory.learned: Most of the feel came from a handful of small physics rules, not from the drawing. The drawing had its own limit: the sand picture is rebuilt every frame, and painting each grain as 3 by 3 pixels crashed the emulator's GL driver after a minute of pouring, so it stays one pixel per grain.

name: Mini Cenários
tagline: Unpack the moving box and decorate tiny rooms, one piece at a time.
description: A cozy decorating game inspired by sticker scene books: unpack each room's moving box and arrange tiny isometric rooms, piece by piece.
storeDescription: Mini Cenários is a cozy room decorating game inspired by the sticker scene books. Each of its eight rooms arrives in a moving box: tap the box to take the next piece out, drag it onto the floor or the wall, turn it and set small decor on tables, desks and the bed. Every room has six tasks, such as turning the TV toward the sofa, that pay coins, and finishing them opens the next room. In free mode you create your own rooms with no tasks, and the gallery keeps every room to share as a picture. Your rooms stay on your phone, coins are never sold, rewarded ads are only shown when you ask for one, and one optional Premium purchase opens everything and removes them.

features.title: A moving box per room
features.description: Eight rooms, from the living room to the garden and a gamer room. Each one arrives in a box with its own pieces, and you take them out one tap at a time.

features.title: Drag, turn, stack
features.description: Drag pieces anywhere they fit, turn them to face where you want, and set mugs, books, a lamp or a sleeping cat on tables, desks and the bed. Undo is one tap away.

features.title: Tasks that pay coins
features.description: Each room has six goals, like a rug under the bed or the TV facing the sofa. Every task pays coins, and meeting all of them opens the next room.

features.title: Shop, walls and floors
features.description: Spend coins on more than 100 pieces, pets and new colours of the sofa, armchair and bed, and change the wall and floor patterns of any room.

features.title: Free mode and gallery
features.description: Create your own rooms in three sizes with no tasks, keep every room in the gallery and share it as a picture.

buildStory.problem: I wanted a phone version of the sticker scene books, the ones where you build a small 3D room by placing stickers, with the unpacking loop of games like Unbox the Room and none of the timers.
buildStory.solution: A Flutter app where every piece of furniture is a small Python script that draws it in isometric SVG, front and back, and writes an index with its footprint and how it turns. The app reads that index instead of keeping its own copy, so the drawing and the placement rules cannot disagree. A CustomPainter draws each room back to front by sorting the footprints, and the music box loop and sound effects are synthesized by a script, so there is no licence to track.
buildStory.learned: Draw order was harder than it looks. Back views needed every shape re-sorted by depth, and pieces had to be sorted by footprint, never by hand. The other lesson was about the tasks: new pieces used to land in spots that met a task by chance, so now they arrive by the door, away from any arrangement, because arranging the room is the game.

name: Emoji Memory Jetpack
tagline: Train your brain. Match your emojis.
description: Match similar emojis. Memory game open-source, built with Android Jetpack Compose.
storeDescription: A colourful memory card game built entirely with Jetpack Compose. Flip cards, find the six matching emoji pairs and play again. The cards flip in 3D and shine as you tilt the phone. No longer on Google Play; the source code is on GitHub.

features.title: Emoji Cards
features.description: Six emoji pairs on a four-column board, reshuffled with one tap.

features.title: Jetpack Compose
features.description: Built entirely with Jetpack Compose: declarative UI and 3D flip animations.

features.title: Holographic tilt
features.description: A sheen on the cards follows the phone's tilt, read from the accelerometer.

features.title: Open Source
features.description: Full source code under the MIT licence. Learn how a small Android game is built with Compose.

buildStory.problem: I wanted to practice MVVM architecture and Jetpack Compose with a real, shipped project, not just a tutorial exercise.
buildStory.solution: A memory card game inspired by iagocavalcante/memorize, rebuilt from scratch in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose and a clean MVVM structure.
buildStory.learned: Managing game state through a ViewModel feels different from regular UI state: the ViewModel becomes the game engine, not just a data holder.

name: Petmob
tagline: Find the best care for your pet.
description: Find the best pet care provider near you, or register as a service provider and earn extra income.
storeDescription: Petmob connects pet owners with service providers in their area: grooming, vet visits, boarding, walks and more. Love animals? Register as a provider and start earning on your own schedule.

features.title: Find Providers
features.description: Search for pet services near you: grooming, vet, boarding, walks and more.

features.title: Earn Extra Income
features.description: Register as a provider and start serving pets in your area on your own schedule.

features.title: Verified Reviews
features.description: Choose providers based on real reviews from other pet owners in your area.

features.title: Easy Scheduling
features.description: Book services directly in the app with instant confirmation.

buildStory.problem: Finding a reliable pet caregiver is hard. Most recommendations still happen by word of mouth.
buildStory.solution: A pet services marketplace connecting owners and providers with ratings, scheduling, and integrated payments.
buildStory.learned: The biggest challenge in local services marketplaces is the bootstrap problem: the app only has value when there's density on both sides.
